query: What material family and specific property are targeted for improvement in face-centered cubic (fcc) high-entropy alloys derived from the Fe-Co-Ni system, and what is the primary scientific challenge regarding the orbital moment contribution to this property in the current state of the art?

generation.hypothesis: The face-centered cubic (fcc) high-entropy alloys derived from the Fe-Co-Ni system will exhibit improved mechanical properties, such as strength and ductility, due to the formation of a random solid solution and simple crystal structure.
generation.material_initial_state: Face-centered cubic (fcc) high-entropy alloys derived from the Fe-Co-Ni system
generation.intervention: High-entropy alloy design using multiple principal elements
generation.conditions: Equiatomic or near-equiatomic composition, high mixing entropy
generation.structural_mediator: Random solid solution and simple crystal structure
generation.mechanism: Solid solution strengthening, grain boundary strengthening, and precipitation strengthening
generation.predicted_outcome: Improved mechanical properties, such as strength and ductility
generation.baseline: Traditional alloys with one or two principal elements
generation.boundary: Limited to high-entropy alloys with specific composition and crystal structure
generation.uncertainty: The exact relationship between the orbital moment contribution and the targeted property is not well understood

falsification_experiment.design: Comparison of mechanical properties between fcc high-entropy alloys and traditional alloys
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the fcc high-entropy alloys do not exhibit improved mechanical properties compared to traditional alloys, the hypothesis is falsified
